newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent, NYMEX given boost by weather.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent, NYMEX given boost by weather.

text.p: Crude futures were firmer on Monday in late Asian trading boosted by worries about cold weather sweeping the U.S. northeast.
February Brent climbed 16 cents to $24.50 per barrel from London trading Friday. March was up 18 cents at $24.02 compared with London on Friday.
Brokers said the February contract was expiring Thursday and had prompted some players to switch long positions to March and so squeeze the front spread.
NYMEX February crude on ACCESS was last traded at $26.30 per barrel, up 21 cents from New York, but February heating oil as high as 73.25 cents per gallon -- up 1.10 from New York.
By late afternoon a weaker-than-expected opening on London gas oil futures cut heating oil back from 73.25 to 73.00 to show a gain on the day of 0.85 cent.
February gas oil on the IPE was down 25 cents at $226.00 per tonne after being called up $1.50 to $2.50.
Brokers said NYMEX crude had held above $26.00 in New York, which had helped the upside on ACCESS Monday, but they said volume was light and might not reflect true market sentiment.
